title: governor config file
description: The shape of governor's config file, .github/governor.json, for an editor to complete and check keys while the file is written. It covers the shape only: it leaves out the rules across keys and the checks on a prompt's text or a prompt file's path, and cannot read prompt files, so a file it accepts can still be refused. The config check, the reusable workflow .github/workflows/config-check.yml in t-d-d/gh-governor, is the full check.

$schema.description: The URL of this file's JSON Schema, for an editor to describe and check each key. Governor ignores it. Use the schema at the commit the config check is pinned to, and bump both together.

environment.description: The claude.ai cloud environment the repo's sessions start in: its name as `/remote-env` lists it, or its ID. A public repo should use the name.

trust.description: `{ "start": [ … ], "auto": [ … ], "task": [ … ], "relay": [ … ], "review": [ … ] }`: whose GitHub text governor acts on, by `author_association`. `start` is who may set work going, by readying a ticket or writing a summons, default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`, which a repo may narrow and never widen. `auto` is whose issues and PRs governor sets going by itself, default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`. `task` is whose issue or PR may become work when a person readies it or summons a session on it, default the same three. `relay` is whose text may reach a running session, default those three and `BOT`. `review` is whose pull requests the PR review reads, default the three.

start.description: Who may set work going, by `author_association`: whose ready label counts, and whose summons starts a session. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`. A repo may narrow it, never widen it: any other value, and `BOT`, is refused.

auto.description: Whose issues and PRs governor sets going by itself, with no person choosing the ticket, by `author_association`: a spec session or owner message when a ticket's wait ends or its blocker closes, a periodic's issue counts and listings, and the conflicts check. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`, narrowed to fit `task`, `relay` and `review` where the file sets them. `BOT` is refused.

task.description: Whose issue or PR may become work when a person sets it going, by `author_association`: pickup starts a ready ticket, and a summons starts a session, only where its author is listed. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`, narrowed to fit `relay` and `review` where the file sets them. `BOT` is refused.

relay.description: Whose text may reach a session that is already running, by `author_association`, with `BOT` for any account GitHub marks as a bot: their comments and reviews, and a session link or `governor:subscribe` line in the body of an issue or PR they open. An event such as a label, a close or a push is judged by the author of the issue or PR it is on. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR` and `BOT`, less any of the first three a `trust.review` the file sets leaves out. Governor's own App is never judged.

review.description: Whose pull requests governor's PR review reads, by `author_association`, with `BOT` for any account GitHub marks as a bot. A pull request by an author it leaves out gets a `neutral` `governor` check, and a person merges it. Dependabot's pull requests are read by `prReview.dependabot` whatever it says. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`.

workflows.description: What the repo's workflows are to governor: `ci`.

ci.description: The CI workflow's file, under `.github/workflows/`. A red run of it tells the sessions of the merges it may blame, and the PR review waits for its run at a PR's head. Without it, no run is CI.

pickup.description: A session per ready ticket, picked up on its label, on the close of its last open blocker, and on the sweep at the interval `sweepHours` sets. Its labels serve the features that read them, so a file turning on `unblocked`, `waits`, `prReview` or `issueReviews` has this section, with `"enabled": false` if pickup is to stay off.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

ready.description: Required when pickup, `unblocked`, `waits`, `prReview` or `issueReviews` is on. Every label a ready ticket carries.

claim.description: Required when pickup, `unblocked`, `waits`, `prReview` or `issueReviews` is on. The label governor claims a ticket with before its session starts. It is created in a repo that lacks it. A ticket carrying it is never picked up.

claimRemoves.description: The ready labels the claim takes off, and a failed launch puts back. Default none.

exclude.description: Labels that keep a ticket out: a ticket carrying any of them is never picked up, and a blocker's close starts no session for it. It cannot name a ready label. Default `["type: prd"]`. A hold label, one that marks a ticket as needing a person or staying not ready (`mode: human`, say), belongs here, or a blocker's close starts a session to rewrite that ticket's spec.

sweepHours.description: How many whole hours the hourly fire leaves between two sweeps of the repo's ready tickets, at least one. Default one, which sweeps at every fire.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

prompt.description: Replaces the default wording of a pickup session's opening prompt, below `Pickup #N 'title'`. It may name the facts {issue}, {repo} and {claim}, which governor writes in. The text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

summons.description: A session per `@claude` remark, and a dispatch started by hand.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

prMessages.description: Messages into the session a PR names, or the newest live session holding its branch.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

subscribeMessages.description: Messages to sessions subscribed by a `governor:subscribe` line, and to an issue's filer. On a claimed ticket, a comment, a close and a reopen also reach the sessions building it, and each message names the ticket's spec owner and builders. A ticket's spec owner, and its builders where it is claimed, hear of its first deploy to each target through governor's comment on it, which asks them to sign off where the issue is closed, and then get no PR deploy message for it. It hears a `deployed:` label only through a subscribe line for `deploys`.

prompt.description: Replaces the default wording of a CI or deploy notice's ask to a subscriber. It may name no fact. The text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

redScheduledRun.description: A fresh session on a scheduled run on the default branch that went red.

unblocked.description: What a blocker's close does to a ticket that is not ready to pick up: a comment when the blocker closed as not planned, a message to a claimed ticket's session, and the spec work on a not-ready ticket. The session whose link ends the ticket's body owns it and is asked to rewrite its own spec; a fresh session rewrites it only where the body names no session or that session is archived, so nobody takes a ticket from its owner.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

ready.description: Replaces the default wording of a ready ticket's ask, below its pickup prompt and the facts of its blocker's close. It may name no fact. The text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

triage.description: The deploy targets whose failure starts one fresh session, rather than messages to the sessions of the merges it shipped. Default none.

tags.description: The tag each deploy target's deploy moves, keyed by target, which deploy messages name. Default none.

deployedLabels.description: Whether a shipping job labels the tickets it shipped `deployed: <target>`, and comments on each ticket the first time it gets that label, so the ticket's spec owner and builders hear of the deploy there in place of a PR message. Default false.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

triage.description: Replaces the default wording of a failed `triage` target's fresh session. It may name no fact. The text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

green.description: Replaces the default wording of a green deploy's ask, for one PR. It may name the facts {pr} and {target}, which governor writes in. The text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

branchRunMessages.description: A run dispatched on a branch tells the session that wrote its commit.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

conflicts.description: A merge into the default branch tells each PR it left conflicted.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

prompt.description: Replaces the default wording of a conflicted PR's ask, to its session or the fallback's. It may name the fact {base}, which governor writes in. The text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

prReview.description: The PR review: its prompt, and the lists it checks a PR against. Needs `prompt` when on.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

prompt.description: Required when on. The review model's system prompt, after governor's fixed frame and before a suffix naming what the code decided: the text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

humanOnly.description: Paths a PR may not change without a person: a PR changing a matching path waits for one, unless every ticket it closes carries one of the entry's `unless` labels and the PR is not from a session governor started. Default none.

glob.description: The paths a PR may not change without a person, as a glob.

reason.description: Why a person must see a change to these paths, which the review says.

unless.description: Labels that waive the wait when every ticket the PR closes carries one and passes the review's ticket checks. They waive nothing for a PR from a session governor started. Default none.

tickets.description: The label rules every ticket the PR closes must meet: `require` and `forbid`.

require.description: Rules each ticket the PR closes meets by carrying one of the rule's labels, unless it carries one of its `unless` labels. Default none.

labels.description: The labels the rule is about.

unless.description: Labels that waive the rule for a ticket carrying one of them. Default none.

forbid.description: Rules each ticket the PR closes meets by carrying none of the rule's labels, unless it carries one of its `unless` labels. Default none.

labels.description: The labels the rule is about.

unless.description: Labels that waive the rule for a ticket carrying one of them. Default none.

quote.description: Globs of changed files the review model reads whole, at the merge base and at the head. Only a modified file is quoted: one added, removed or renamed waits for a person. A `!` entry takes a path back out. Default none.

decides.description: Labels of a ticket that may decide a quoted file's change: its body's first line, `Constraint now lives at <path>, …`, names the files it decides, which then pass unread. Default none.

dependabot.description: Globs of the manifests a Dependabot PR may change and pass with no model. Default none.

requireChecks.description: Checks the review treats as required, beside any the default branch requires on GitHub: a name, which a check run from any App or a commit status context meets, or `{ "name", "app" }`, which only that App's check run of the name meets. One red on the PR's head fails the review for a push; one not finished, or not posted, holds the review with `governor` in progress until it ends. A name GitHub also requires counts once, and the review's own `governor` check is left out. Default none.

app.description: The slug of the GitHub App that must post it, such as `github-actions` or `github-code-scanning`: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, the last part of its `github.com/apps/<slug>` page. A run of the name from any other App, and a commit status of the name, does not count.

waitForCi.description: Whether the review waits for the `workflows.ci` run at the PR's head: one red fails it for a push, one not finished, or none at the head, holds it with `governor` in progress. Set it false where the CI workflow does not run on pull requests, such as one that runs only on a push to the default branch; the review then reads no workflow runs, and still reads the required checks and `requireChecks`. A red CI run on the default branch still drives `ciMessages`. Default true.

merge.description: Whether a pass merges the PR. With false, a pass posts its comment and a success check, and the owner merges. Default true.

heartbeat.description: Governor records each fire on the issue `issue` names: a line for pickup and one per periodic, under the `<!-- governor:heartbeat -->` marker its body must carry. Needs `issue` when on.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

issue.description: Required when on. The number of the issue governor records its fires on. Its body must already carry the `<!-- governor:heartbeat -->` marker, or governor writes nothing into it.

periodics.description: A session per periodic in `sessions`, each time its day limit passes or one of its counts is reached. Needs at least one periodic when on.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

sessions.description: The recurring sessions governor starts on a day limit, or on a count of merges, issues opened or issues closed, each keyed by its name: one line, with no space at either end. Its session is named after it, and governor keys its record by it. At least one when on.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

prompt.description: What the periodic's session runs: the text, or { "file": "<path>" }. Governor adds a line under it giving the last fire's time, and lists what each count counted since then.

days.description: Required. The day limit, in whole days, at least one: the periodic is due on the sweep nearest that many days after its last fire.

counts.description: Counts that bring the periodic due before its day limit, once any reaches its number since the last fire: `merges`, `issuesOpened` and `issuesClosed`. At its day limit, a periodic whose counts counted nothing starts no session.

merges.description: Pull requests merged into the default branch since the last fire that bring the periodic due, a whole number of at least one.

issuesOpened.description: Issues opened since the last fire that bring the periodic due, a whole number of at least one.

issuesClosed.description: Issues closed since the last fire that bring the periodic due, a whole number of at least one.

gapHours.description: The fewest whole hours between two of the periodic's runs, at least one. A count reached inside the gap fires on the first event or sweep after it.

connectors.description: The claude.ai connectors the periodic's session needs, each named once by its name in the account's connector list. A periodic naming any starts as a run of a routine governor keeps for it, with those connectors attached and no others.

hooks.description: A session on a hook's prompt when a signed request fires one of the hooks `sessions` holds. A fire while the hook's last session is open goes into that session as a message. Needs at least one hook when on.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

sessions.description: The sessions an outside system starts with a signed request, each keyed by its name: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. The name ends the hook's URL, and its session is named after it. Each may cap its fires with `perHour`. At least one when on.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

prompt.description: What the hook's session runs: the text, or { "file": "<path>" }. Governor adds lines under it saying which hook fired and when, and quoting the caller's text as the caller's data.

keyVersion.description: Required. The version of the hook's key a request must be signed with, a positive whole number of at most nine digits. Raising it revokes the key before it. It is not a secret.

perHour.description: The most fires governor queues for the hook in one clock hour, a positive whole number up to 100. A fire past it gets 429. Default 20.

waits.description: When a ticket's `Blocked until:` date passes and it is not ready, one comment saying the wait ended, and, if `unblocked` is on, its spec work, which goes to its owner first as a blocker's close does. Every session governor starts is told how to make a ticket wait. The hold itself needs no switch.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

issue.description: The number of the wait ticket: governor links each waiting ticket as blocked by it, and removes the link when the wait ends. An issue can block at most 50. Without it, governor links nothing.

prompts.description: Replacement wording for the instruction in each kind of message the feature sends, keyed by kind: `spec`, `ownerSpec`.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

spec.description: Replaces the default wording of a not-ready ticket's spec session's ask, below the facts of its ended wait. It may name the facts {issue}, {ready} and {claim}, which governor writes in. The text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

ownerSpec.description: Replaces the default wording of the ask to a not-ready ticket's owner, the session its body names, below the facts of its ended wait. It may name the facts {issue}, {ready} and {claim}, which governor writes in. The text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

signOff.description: Governor archives an idle session in the repo whose last reply ends `Signing off.`, and a message about a close or a deploy, with nothing else open, asks the session to sign off.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on. Default on: only `false` turns it off, and then the section needs none of its required settings.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

prompt.description: Replaces the default wording of the standing line's ask to sign off. It may name no fact. The text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

issueReviews.description: The issue reviews: `reviews`, each keyed by its name, with its selector `when`, the labels each of its `conclusions` adds, and optionally its own `prompt` and checks and labels per label (`byLabel`), and `enabled`. Each comments on a ticket it selects whether it passes, waits for an edit, or waits for a person, and applies that conclusion's labels. Governor runs them where the file has this section, unless `enabled` is `false`.

enabled.description: Whether governor runs the reviews. Default on: only `false` turns them off.

reviews.description: The issue reviews, each keyed by its name: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. The name goes into every comment and marker the review writes, so renaming a review starts its rounds afresh. Reviews run in the order of their keys. At least one when on.

when.description: The review's selector: the labels and authors a ticket must meet. Default every issue its default `by` lets in.

labels.description: Labels the ticket must carry, every one of them, in any case. Default none.

exclude.description: Labels the ticket must not carry, any of them, in any case. Default none.

by.description: Who may have opened the ticket, as GitHub's `author_association` values. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`. The repo's `trust.review` bounds every review.

conclusions.description: The labels each conclusion adds: `success`, `failure` and `neutral`, each a list, each none when unset. Each run adds its conclusion's labels and removes the ones the other two name, and touches no other label. Each label starts with the review's name, a colon and a space, such as `triage: build` for a review named `triage`, in any case, so a review never adds or removes a label a person uses. A label appears under one conclusion of one review. A review whose `by`, within `trust.review`, reaches beyond `trust.auto` names no ready label. No conclusion names a label a `byLabel` entry matches on, a label the review's own `when.labels` or `when.exclude` names, or `pickup.claim`.

success.description: The labels a `success` adds: the ticket passes. Default none.

failure.description: The labels a `failure` adds: the ticket waits for an edit by whoever filed it. Default none.

neutral.description: The labels a `neutral` adds: the ticket waits for a person. Default none.

prompt.description: The review's own prompt, after governor's fixed frame: the text, or { "file": "<path>" }. Default governor's own checklist.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

byLabel.description: Checks and labels per label, each entry matched by label. A ticket gets the review's prompt and then each matching entry's, in list order; one matching none gets the review's alone. For each conclusion, the labels come from the first matching entry that names it, and otherwise from `conclusions`.

labels.description: The labels that match a ticket carrying any of them, in any case. At least one.

prompt.description: Checks a matching ticket gets after the review's own prompt: the text, or { "file": "<path>" }. Default none.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

conclusions.description: The conclusions whose labels this entry overrides, each a list, each label starting with the review's name, a colon and a space. A conclusion it leaves out takes its labels from an entry later in the list that matches, or from the review's `conclusions`.

success.description: The labels a `success` adds on a matching ticket, in place of the review's.

failure.description: The labels a `failure` adds on a matching ticket, in place of the review's.

neutral.description: The labels a `neutral` adds on a matching ticket, in place of the review's.
